Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: No evidence of operational CRVS integration with a data exchange platform. The National Agency for People Registry issues birth certificates and manages civil registration, but no documented API-level integration with other government systems or a data exchange hub. The e-ID pilot notes 44% of population in rural areas with limited services. Score 2: planned.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with the Comments field, which itself proposed 'Score 2: planned'. Verification found stronger evidence than either: ANRPTS (the agency managing both civil registration and the population registry) has exposed web APIs since c.2010 used by the national election commission, mobile operators and financial institutions for identity verification (UNDP/ANRPTS, 2021), and a 2024 government-commissioned scoping study (Sofrecom, for MTNIMA) names 'état civil et papiers d'identité' as one of the first service families for a planned cross-government API gateway/data platform, alongside the 2022 National Strategy for Open and Interoperable Data. This supports 'Under development' (3) rather than Unknown or the previously suggested 'Planned' (2). No full operational data-exchange integration is yet confirmed.
revised_comments: Mauritania's National Agency for People Registry and Secure Documents (ANRPTS) manages both civil registration and the biometric population registry, and has offered web APIs since around 2010 that allow authorised external bodies — including the national election commission, mobile network operators and financial institutions — to verify identity in real time. A 2024 government-commissioned scoping study for the Ministry of Digital Transformation identifies civil-status and identity documents as one of the first service families to be brought into a planned cross-government API gateway and unified data platform, building on the 2022 National Strategy for Open and Interoperable Data. Full integration of CRVS data into a unified national data exchange is under development but not yet operational.

revised_comments: There is no documented evidence that Mauritania's electoral register is integrated into a wider government data exchange for demographic analysis or service-delivery targeting. The national election commission draws on the ANRPTS population/civil registry via a web API for identity-verification purposes, but this reflects the electoral authority's one-way use of civil-registry data rather than integration of the electoral register itself into cross-government data infrastructure. Mauritania's broader data-exchange architecture remains at an early, largely non-operational stage.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No documented operational integration of employment/labor services with a data exchange platform. Score 2: planned within broader digital transformation agenda.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with Comments stating 'Score 2: planned'. Verification found more recent, concrete evidence: Mauritania launched the 'Mourchid' digital platform (26 June 2026) centralising public youth-employment, training and entrepreneurship programmes under the Ministry of Youth Empowerment, Employment, Sports and Civic Service. This is a live, functioning consolidation platform (beyond merely 'planned'), though it currently serves mainly as an information/guidance portal rather than a fully interoperable job-seeker registry linked to the wider data exchange; a Social Registry and the National Employment Agency (ANE) database are referenced together for beneficiary targeting in donor programmes but no API-level integration with the cross-government exchange is documented. Revised to 'Under development' (3).
revised_comments: Mauritania launched the 'Mourchid' digital platform in June 2026, centralising public employment, vocational-training and entrepreneurship-support programmes run by the Ministry of Youth Empowerment, Employment, Sports and Civic Service into a single online portal. The platform currently functions mainly as an information and guidance tool rather than a fully interoperable job-seeker registry: a separate Social Registry and the National Employment Agency (ANE, formerly ANAPEJ) database exist and are referenced together for beneficiary targeting in donor-funded youth-employment programmes, but no API-level integration between employment services and the wider cross-government data exchange has been documented. Integration is under development but not yet operational.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: No documented operational integration of Mauritanian tax/revenue systems with a data exchange platform. The National Digital Transformation Agenda mentions transparency and e-government improvements but no specific tax authority API integration documented. Score 2: planned.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with Comments stating 'Score 2: planned'. Verification found stronger evidence of actual (if partial) integration: the 'Khidmaty' platform now bundles new business creation into a single online transaction that simultaneously completes commercial-registry enrolment, tax registration and CNSS affiliation across three separate agencies — genuine operational cross-agency data integration for this transaction type. The DGI's 2025-2029 strategic plan additionally commits to further 'interfaçage' between the DGI's information system and other public entities and to generalising e-filing/e-payment, indicating integration is ongoing but not yet comprehensive. Revised to 'Partially integrated' (4).
revised_comments: Mauritania's tax authority (Direction Générale des Impôts) operates an online portal (impots.gov.mr) for tax declaration, taxpayer-file consultation, NIF verification and tax-clearance certificates. Since 2026 the 'Khidmaty' government-services platform has integrated new-business creation into a single online transaction that simultaneously completes commercial-registry enrolment, tax registration and Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS) affiliation, demonstrating genuine cross-agency data integration for this transaction type. The DGI's 2025-2029 strategic plan sets out further planned actions to interface its information system with other public entities and to generalise electronic tax filing and payment, indicating that integration of tax and revenue systems into a unified data exchange is partial rather than comprehensive.

revised_comments: Mauritania's social-protection digitisation is under active development. The Caisse Nationale de Solidarité en Santé (CNASS) signed a cooperation agreement with the State Digital Agency (AN-ETAT) in July 2025 to digitise its health-insurance infrastructure as part of a 2025-2030 digitisation strategy, and launched initial digital services for policyholders on the 'Khidmati' platform in May 2026. Separately, CNSS (social-security) affiliation has been integrated into the unified online business-registration transaction on the 'Khidmaty' platform, evidencing some operational cross-agency data flow. Comprehensive integration of social-assistance programmes, grant registries and beneficiary-management systems into a single national data exchange has not yet been documented.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence of AI integrated into government data exchange systems. Mauritania launched a National AI Strategy 2025-2029 and the Digital Watch Observatory confirms this strategy exists. However, the e-ID pilot, Khdamati platform, and Ijraati portal have no documented AI capabilities for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics. The country ranks 165th in the 2024 UN EGDI with particularly low online services scores. Score 1: no AI integration in data exchange.

revised_comments: Mauritania has adopted a National AI Strategy (2025-2029), reflecting broader ambitions for artificial intelligence in the public sector, but there is no documented evidence that AI or machine-learning capabilities have been integrated into the government's data exchange, the Ijraati administrative-procedures portal or the Khdamati/Khidmaty service platforms for data-quality assurance, fraud detection or predictive analytics. The country's e-government maturity remains comparatively low (165th of 193 countries in the UN 2024 E-Government Development Index, score 0.3491), consistent with the absence of advanced analytics capabilities in government systems.

revised_comments: No evidence has been found of provincial or local government participation in a data-exchange or interoperability platform in Mauritania; digital-reform activity is concentrated at the central-government level through the Ministry of Digital Transformation and its Ijraati/Khidmaty portals, along with sectoral agencies such as the DGI, CNASS and CNSS. Forty-four percent of the population lives in rural areas with comparatively limited connectivity and public-service infrastructure, and rural mobile-broadband coverage lags well behind urban areas (2023 national coverage data show 2G at 97%, 3G at 43.9% and 4G at 34.7%), reinforcing the concentration of digital-government initiatives at the centre.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: Mauritania has a data protection law (Law No. 2017-020, though not yet in force) and has ratified the AU Malabo Convention. A Personal Data Protection Authority (APD) exists. The National Strategy for Open and Interoperable Data (2022) promotes transparency and alignment with Open Government Partnership principles. The Ijraati portal includes an administrative dashboard and statistical tracking. However, the 2017 DPA has not yet come into effect. Score 2: low/limited disclosure with policy commitments in place.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (2) is consistent with the Comments and confirmed on review. Additional verification: Law No. 2017-020 on personal data protection is in force (enacted 2017), with the Data Protection Authority (APD) established and pursuing enforcement per its 2023-2026 strategic plan (contrary to the original comment's claim that the law is 'not yet in force'). A general open-data catalogue (DataMR, ~100 datasets) already exists, and a dedicated national open-data portal (data.gov.mr) is scheduled for delivery March-April 2026 under the WARDIP project. However, no public dashboard, annual report or published data-sharing agreements specific to the data-exchange system's own governance and operations were found. Confirmed at 'Low - Limited Disclosure' (2); the redteam flag on Value Name/scale-label mismatch is cosmetic and does not affect the score.
revised_comments: Mauritania has enacted personal-data-protection legislation (Law No. 2017-020) and established a Data Protection Authority (APD), which is pursuing enforcement capacity-building under its 2023-2026 strategic plan, and has ratified the African Union's Malabo Convention. A general open-data catalogue (DataMR) already publishes around 100 datasets, and a dedicated national open-data portal (data.gov.mr) is being developed under the WARDIP programme with delivery expected in early 2026. The 'Ijraati' administrative-procedures portal includes an internal dashboard for public administrations and statistical tracking of procedures. However, no public dashboard, annual report or published data-sharing agreements specific to the governance and operations of the cross-government data exchange itself have been identified, placing public transparency at a low, limited-disclosure level.
